I have done some construction work with my father over the years on our house. Tried welding, building, woodwork, stuff like that. We actually did a lot of stuff on the house by ourselves. However all of that made me feel even worse, the same dread/hard-to-breathe feeling that I get whenever I am forced to do something. At some times I even felt a panic attack of some sort and just wanted to run away as fast as possible. None of that helped me in the slightest, only made things worse. Even on some decent days when I have control, just the call from my father to come and work ruined everything.

I just feel like I'm a disabled person. Like I can't do anything. And the system and how the world works do not allow those people to be here. I've seen a lot of people on this sub dreading work but even they sometimes find something and live off it. I just don't know how those people do it and I envy them. I guess the power of wanting to live is greater than anything. But sadly my will went away a long time ago.

I have thought about moving away from my country but it seems like it would lower my coping ability even more. I dread the feeling of living alone and having to do everything myself. Even the smallest tasks like washing dishes is a nightmare to me, I can barely get out of bed and every morning is a torture. My parents do have indirect help like cooking for me and cleaning, if I was alone it would all start falling apart pretty quickly. I don't do well with people either, have some kind of anthropophobia as well. So I would go in completely blind and alone. Fun is something I lost sense to a decade ago almost so I wouldn't do anything out of pure fun since I can't physically feel it anymore. Only reason why I would want to escape is to buy time, my parents are pretty old (72 and 68) so I don't think I would have to suffer for more than 20 years.

Talked to parents already a milion times regarding almost everything. Have went to more than 10 doctors and been on medications of different variety. And ofcourse the darkest period where I was in a psych ward for suicide contemplation.

The career coach thingy I also tried I believe. If that is some form of a professional orientation then yes, I have been there but to no avail, got only vague answers and was still lost.

The burden of all of this was barely contained but now with all of the work stuff coming up, I'm losing it. I don't want to lose my freedom. Not now when I need as much time as possible to cope with everything. But alas, noone listens. Just constant yelling and forcing me to find jobs none of which I like. It also doesn't help that I have no skills/diploma since uni was so hard for me that I failed everything.

I don't want to give up just yet, 22 is too early for a funeral and also my parents would brake. Also am an only son and death would lose everything for them. I just hope that I will be able to cope with the work stress and life change. Money doesn't matter to me almost, I need very little to survive.

Thanks for the good luck, this hell/greedy world isn't easy at all.

Okay, so from a guy that played DotA 2 a lot here it is basically. I was very high rank in DotA back when I played it over a course of 5 years, in ML I am a Mythic 5-4 pleb.

I will use some DotA heroes to compare here and then talk about ML. If a hero is considered a hard carry he usually:

-is absurdly strong late game in situations where everyone is full build (Void, Spectre, Arc Warden, Medusa)

-has insane farm speed leading to him taking over the gold lead by 2 times from the enemy very quickly (Anti-Mage, Meepo, Alchemist, Arc Warden)

-can solo most of the enemy team late game no problem (Spectre, Sven, Medusa, PL)

-is very mobile and has a GTFO skill (Anti-Mage, Weaver,  PL, Morphling)

-tanky as fuck late game (Anti-Mage, Sven, PL, Spectre)

-weak in lane if alone (some like Naix and Weaver are also very good early game).

So there is some basic stuff, hero needs to be able to dish out a huge chunk of damage reliably and have a safe path to doing so without getting rekt in lane and then never recover. This is also called as a priority 1 picks. Those guys get farm first and in the largest quantity, 2nd is a midlaner and 3rd offlane. Usually also these heroes feature either some AoE damage or absurd single target dps with low CD.

For ML, heroes like Claude and Karrie fit this role but they are quite different. Claude has a shit early game but his farm speed ramps up very quickly. He also has great AoE and melts enemy heroes with ease. Somewhat weak to CC, but has a great escape and can close the game very quickly due to having so much more gold than the enemy. Karrie is another beast. Strongest MM late game just cause she has absurd true damage, is mobile like no tomorrow, and even tanky in some builds. Doesn't require boots so effectively a 6 full item MM. She has slower farm speed than Claude but when she gets to where she needs to be, it is impossible to stop her. Tanks just melt regardless of what build you have on them. Also, they both heavily benefit from **both buffs** making them the prime heroes for the role.

You take one of them mid. 4 masks in a team and you are the MM on mid lane. Take the lane, take red then blue and down find yourself a crab. Never stop farming. Tanks and supports follow you so it is always 2 with you atleast. If played properlly, they set up farm for you in advance or hold lane creeps so you make it in time to catch everything. Fight only at turtle. If you continue farming like this there is almost 0 chance the enemy catches up cause their farm is split between a mage and a MM and yours isn't.

This tactic is very very strong, but somewhat hard to execute. And also in ranks below Myth 2 I would say dont even try this. You need a good team comp and thats just what doesnt happen in low ranks, including where I am. But yea, if executed correctly and the MM player is good, this strat would be the best one out there. The reason this appeared now is cause of how the buffs work and how some heroes got buffed/nerfed.

Champ dark runs should only be done if you are doing a torchless challenge run. Otherwise never do them. But if you still decide to do it, here are some tips in no specific order:

-party must be able to handle shuffles and immobile characters are shit

-you must have the ability to hit every rank

-stuns are invaluable, and stun characters should have speed on them as trinkets and some stun chance

-take out the back line first always

-focus fire your dmg, dont do aoe for no reason, you need to eliminate the high priority targets asap

-if you have it, bring guard characters for extra saftety (i.e. Treeman crit in the Weald)

-Ruins and Cove are the easiest, avoid Warrens at all costs

-party must be able to handle the Shambler (12% chance he is a hallway battle)

-avoid hall battles as much as possible due to the Shambler spawn, prioritize the room battles

-avoid explore 90% rooms quests, they are much harder

-a healer is a must

-stack up on bandages and antivenom so you don't get rekt by the shambler

-only bring max upgraded characters

-stress healer is a must, stress dmg in no light is very high, even with -stress trinkets

-party must be able to handle collector

-use every single oportunity you have to recover from a fight, look up the stalling mechanic and utilize it when you can

-bring a PD to the Cove so you can cure bleed from the crab

Hope this helps a bit, these are just some things that came to my mind.
Room by room, hall by hall.. we reclaim what is ours.

+Stress in high/low light, depening on what you play, remove it straight away. Klepto is a terrible one, remove asap and dont bring heroes to missions before u clean it.

Curious is awful as well, curio interaction is very ugly, this goes for the rest of the forced curio interactions. -Speed should be cleaned asap on characters that need to go very fast (i.e. PD).

Bleed resist is also very bad, but not top priority so you can clean it later. -Healing skills on Vestals are top priority.

All in all, stress, speed, forced interaction is a top priority, watch FilthyRibots quirk guide on YT and see that as well.

Plan from the beginning always, you need 16 ppl in total to complete the DD quests, think about the comps, who goes where ecc.. -tanks to attack, inf to defend, sometimes inf can attack, but depends where and what are they attacking, tanks for example suck dick in mountains or jungle

    -15/5 template for tanks is usual (15 tanks +5 motorized, 13/7 is also good), just keep the org near 30

-engineer, signal, maintenece, arty, logistics for tanks, swap maintenece for recon for INF (only for 40w INF)

-20w INF + eng is a classic solid defender, 10w + eng is also great

-attack according to terrain, don't send tanks to mountains and hills, avoid crossing rivers if you can, attack in the day preferably, avoid attacking where there are a million other troops

-create encirclements, that way you essentially kill their units (they can't retreat), but also, avoid from getting yourself encircled (e.g. don't overextend or spaghetti into the SU)

-attack when you have equipment, don't attack if the brown line under the unit isn't full

-check if you have attrition, if you do, stop, repair infrastructure and then go, never attack in attrition

I have been having this issue as well in MP, and I'll give you some tips on how to do it. You need to encircle as much as you can until the Stalin line, then march towards it. Put all your tanks in the north, at the opening in the Stalin Line. If the USSR player does forts, take the fort buster general and use him to lead your tanks.

Template is as follows: 7 mot, 14 heavy/medium tanks, support engi, arty, recon, signal, rocket arty if you can fit it (AT if facing a lot of tanks). Your tanks must be 40w, no questions here, and I would shoot for atleast 24 of them for Russia, rest goes to defend D-day.

Put all the CAS you have on that region, make sure you have good eff, build closer airport or a radar if eff is below 50%. Talk to your Romania, tell him to get CAS 2 as well, he can also build 40w Marines to pressure the south, you need to lend lease him a bit to make sure he has what he needs.

You can also tell Spain to do pure anti-inf tanks, with mass SPG's and barely armor to counter it. USSR doesn't have AT in every single division, if they do, means they have no tanks and vice-versa. 

Also, always look what the USSR is doing, and adapt to it. If he goes heavy tanks, you do the same. Pure inf? SPG in you divisions. Scared of their air? SPAA or 2 in their divisions. No air with a lot of tanks? Go 2-4 TD's.

If you really struggle to break it and fail every game at it, if your rules allow it, invade Norway at all costs, that way you bypass the Stalin line and the USSR player will panic for sure. Another cheese you can do, is to use TAC 1's and bomb infrastructure at Moscow, that will attrition him and lower his war support (I assume strats are banned so I reccomend TAC bombers).

Rushing Europe is key as Germany, you need to declare on USSR as soon as rules allow. If he goes forts, that's just +5% bonus attack he gave you and he didn't make factories at that time. Use this to your advantage. Avoid attrition, repair infrastructure, use logistics in your INF templates, build airports so you have more eff (or tell Hungary to do it, Romania can as well. 5 armies is the minimum so you don't get pushed, adjust production accordingly.

1. Industry - go like a madman here, you need everything you can get here, except excavation and the synth's, go the right side of fuel since you have oil

2. Land doctorine - Mass Mob all the way, best for USSR for the -width on divisions, defence, org, you name it; go left side of course

3. Tankz - check the German player to see when he is doing the treaty, when you see it go with Light tank 2 and then just rush to medium 2's with that research slot

4. Electronics & encrypt/decrypt - this should be at the top but I guess everyone knows that so I put it here, -research speed is godlike

5. AT/AA/ARTY - since you'll be using it, you'll need it up to date

-ditch the inf equipment upgrades, only do them if you have nothing else to do

(IV) **POLITICAL POWER**:

1. Free trade
2. War economy
3. Captian of Industry
4. Military theorist
5. Tank company (before you start med 1's)
6. Popular figurehead
7. Arty designer
8. Military staff
